Performers
Eric Xi Xin Liang (piano) Documented

Commons credits Liang for performance and recording; the matching IMSLP entry explicitly identifies piano. No flautist is named. The piano-only displayed credit is the documented minimum, not proof that an optional part is absent. No flute entrance or ensemble stage timeline is invented.

[1] [2]
Work version
Unknown Unknown

The performing edition is not identified. Gann discusses both a flute version and Ives’s alternative without flute, but neither recording source specifies which option Liang used. No edition, optional instrument, exact thematic-entry timestamp or bar alignment is inferred from the general history of the sonata.

[1] [2] [3]
Recorded
2024 Documented

The source’s Summary gives 2024 for the performance/recording. The 14 July 2024 file upload does not establish a session day, and a common session with the other movements is not assumed.

No record label is identified. IMSLP credits Eric Xi Xin Liang as the 2024 audio publisher; that is not a named commercial-label credit. Neither source supplies sleeve or label scans.

Transfer
Eric Xi Xin Liang — performance and recording Documented

The source explicitly credits Liang as the recording creator. Uploader D. Benjamin Miller is not thereby a transfer or mastering engineer; no separate engineer is named.

Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

No transfer or mastering date is established. The July 2024 upload and February 2026 Wikimedia transcode dates are not session or transfer dates.

[1]
Processing
Unknown Unknown

No editing, overdubbing, mastering, restoration, noise reduction or source-transfer process is disclosed. The access-file encoding is known, but the original recording chain is not.

[1] [2]
Composition rights
Public domain as asserted in Commons’ separate musical-composition notice Documented

The notice cites Ives’s death in 1954 and publication before 1931, separately from the recording’s licence. Gann distinguishes 1920 printing and January 1921 circulation from the revised 1947 edition. Because the performing edition is unknown, later revisions and editorial additions are not independently cleared here. IMSLP marks the revised score non-public-domain in the United States.

[1] [3] [2]
Recording rights
Rule 1 — explicit sound-recording licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International Documented

The opened Commons page explicitly labels the Recording CC BY 4.0 and names Liang as performance/recording creator. The separate composition public-domain notice is not used as the recording licence. IMSLP’s matching audio entry also states CC BY 4.0. Attribution and a licence link are required; the 2024 recording is not claimed to be public domain.

Charles Ives, Piano Sonata No. 2, ‘Concord, Mass., 1840–⁠60’, IV. Thoreau — Eric Xi Xin Liang, piano and recording (2024). Recording licensed CC BY 4.0.
